CHAPTER FOUR: CLASSES & RACES
Section One: Redefining Classes

Much like how the worlds of D&D are home to many classes of character, so too is the Milky Way. All the standard classes of D&D still exist in space, but most of them are tweaked or adapted to better fit the space environment. Below, we will discuss all the regular classes and how they change to better fit the space setting
Important Note:

Before we discuss classes, we must first discuss a few notable statistical changes made to the core game. For one, the Arcana skill will be changed to be Technology. In the Milky Way, some technology is so advanced it may be mistaken for magic, but true magic does not exist. As such, the Arcana skill has been realigned to allow the skill to fit this universe’s version of magic. Because D&D beyond does not allow you to overhaul skill types, within the App the skill will remain Arcana, but do know that from here forward that skill is Technology.

Second, a few new proficiencies have been added. Once again, they cannot be added directly into the D&D Beyond app, so keeping track of these proficiencies will need to be done differently, either within the app or not.
The added proficiencies are:
Piloting
Driving
Heavy Firearms
Power Armors
Artificer

The artificer receives very little change. Like usual, they are masters of invention and intellect, which is unsurprisingly very useful in space. They can invent, modify, and alter technology at rapid and fascinating rates.

Technological Services: Artificers can unjam weapons that have suffered misfires without making a check. If the weapon was very damaged, then they must make the regular Tinkering Check, but gain advantage. They are also quite proficient at repairing ships, which manifests at DM discretion.
Barbarians

The barbarian class will be relatively unchanged. The background and lore of a barbarian would be slightly different, a Barbarian perhaps was born on a brutal slave world or a world with dangerous wildlife and learned to be strong.
Bard

The Bard class will also be quite similar to before but with some notable lore changes. Because magic does not exist in space, any class involving magic will be very different. Rather than Bards being magical, they are one of two classes that are Psions. For more information on Psions and Psionics, see the Lore of the Galaxy document, but put simply they have a special genetic mutation that allows them to draw on power from another dimension.
Bards in space still are charismatic musicians who inspire allies, but now they have the added feature of being a special genetic mutant who can access the Psyscape.

Psionic Amplification: When within melee range of any other Psion, both Psions gain +1d6 to all rolls of all types. This is because the psionic energy of Psions is powerful and can be tapped into by other Psions.
Cleric

The cleric, like a lot of other classes, only changes majorly in the Lore sense. Rather than calling upon a holy being or some other deity, Clerics, more often just called Battle Medics, use advanced medicine technology to heal their ally, and similarly powerful offensive technology to harm their enemies.

Another major difference for the Cleric class is in space is that it has a less Melee focused approach and shifts to be more Ranged. Clerics are proficient with Power Armor by default, a result of training with the armor for battle medicine applications.
Druid

The Druid is one of the most vastly different classes in space. Rather than calling upon elemental powers and nature as they do in core rules, Druids are a special race of shapeshifting aliens that have very powerful control over their bodies ability to transform. For simplicity, this race of aliens are called ‘The Druids’. They hail from the planet Druidaia, a shadowy and strange world in the galactic east

It is very common for Druids to choose a full identity to portray in regular life. They have no ‘true’ or ‘natural’ shape, so it is up to them to decide who they want to be in daily life. This means that when selecting the Druid class, you still choose a regular race and appearance to take on. This will be the form that your character chooses to use as their identity when not shapeshifting to something else.

As a result of this Lore change, Druids can now shapeshift into any living creature, not just animals as is true in core rules. While this may seem very powerful, there are some major considerations to keep in mind. The Druids are very good at altering their physical appearance, but are not nearly as good at mimicking actions or behaviors. A druid who shapeshifts to act as another type of humanoid may look very convincing, but without lots of practice will fail to move, speak, or act in a way that is convincing to others. This presents an opportunity for druids to practice and specialize humanoid mimicry, but does not make their class an outright master of infiltration. It is up to the player and DM to agree on what forms practice might take, how long it might take to get practice, and what level of control the Druid has. Below are the four levels of practice and mastery a druid may have at imitating another humanoid.
When mimicking a humanoid race other than their race identity:
No Practice: All Charisma based checks made with disadvantage
Some Practice: All Charisma based checks made with a -5 penalty
Well Practiced: All Charisma based checks made with a -2 Penalty
Mastery: Regular Checks
When it comes to mimicking a non-humanoid creature, all standard rules for Druids apply as usual.
Fighter

Fighters are mostly unchanged, however skill and development into the use of firearms is an added bonus of their class. Many fighters were/are some form of well trained soldier somewhere in the galaxy, and as such have prowess in both melee and ranged weaponry.
The existing Gunslinger subclass will work well as a template for space fighters.
Monk

The monk also is relatively unchanged. In space, many monks will pursue forms of cybernetic alteration and enhancement to bring about a better harmony with their bodies and the machines of the world. As such, in addition to all you might think of when you think of monks, space monks also are quite proficient with using and manipulating technology.
All monks are proficient in Technology (Arcana), and have some extra abilities related to manipulating technologies, detailed below.
Hacking Proficiency: Monks have advantage on Technology checks to hack into computer systems.

Jam Systems: Monks within melee range of any technologically advanced item (Computers, robots, advanced energy weapons, etc) can attempt to disrupt the computational systems of that item. This will manifest in different ways, perhaps shutting down a robot or overloading a plasma gun. To do this, an attack and a Technology check (DC is situational) is required

Mechanical learning: Via cybernetic enhancements some monks choose to install within themselves they can access, sort, and interface with massive amounts of digital information quickly. At certain terminals, monks can access information that non-monks could likely not, such as learning the route history of a crashed spaceship, or the name and location of a spy in a government facility.

Monk-Warlock Synergy: Monks and Warlocks work well together as their shared reliance on technology unites them. When together and within melee range of each other, Monks and Warlocks can provide each other +1d6 to any check or save once per long rest each.
Paladin

The paladin receives the most thorough overhaul of any class. Where a regular paladin in D&D is a tanky, close range holy warrior, the new Paladin will be very different. The paladin class is converted into the Heavy Gunner class. This class is built to be a much heavier version of the new Ranger and Fighter classes.

All Paladins are proficient with Heavy Weapons and Power Armor. Though paladins are gunners first and foremost, their heavy armor means they can get close to enemies if needed. Paladins will usually carry some melee weapon as backup, but using massive heavy weapons will usually be their preference

Paladins rely most on Strength and Constitution. Good teamwork will make a Paladin a very dangerous foe, but without a team to support him Paladins can be easily overwhelmed due to their slow, heavy nature.
Ranger

The ranger changes quite a bit conceptually, but in practice not at all. As opposed to a bow and arrow wielding forest guardian, the Ranger in space is a daring gunslinger well trained in the use of precision firearms. Where a fighter gunner might be proficient with medium sized rifles and a Paladin Heavy Gunner uses the bulkiest and heaviest guns, the ranger is most comfortable using light, precision weapons, such as snipers, submachine guns, and pistols. While these are their preferences, Rangers are very comfortable with guns of all types.
Firearm Mastery: Add double your proficiency bonus to attacks using snipers, SMGs, and Pistols.

Sniper Chain: Killing an enemy with a sniper rifle refunds the action used to take the shot, meaning you can fire again beyond your max number of actions as long as you keep getting kills. Reloading still must be taken into account.
Rogue

The rogue is very unchanged from its regular counterpart. Rogues, like in regular D&D, are masters of subterfuge and assasination. This is very useful in space, as Rogues can lend their services to any number or organizations or syndicates and make money doing so.
Suppressor Proficiency: Rogues do not suffer the range and damage penalties of using suppressors.
Sorcerer

The sorcerer is the other Psion class of the galaxy. They call upon the energies of the Psyscape to conjure a vast array of Psionic powers. Born with rare genetic mutations, sorcerers are a rare and valuable type of individual.

Psionic Amplification: When within melee range of any other Psion, both Psions gain +1d6 to all rolls of all types. This is because the psionic energy of Psions is powerful and can be tapped into by other Psions.
Warlock
The warlock receives a fairly significant change. Rather than selling their soul to some deity in a pact, the Warlock of space is a highly modified cyborg who has sold their body to the machine.

Warlocks are Cyborgs. They are individuals who, either purposefully or not, have had massive amounts of their body replaced with advanced and powerful robotics and technology. This allows Warlocks to be a powerful hybrid between melee fighting and high tech ranged weaponry.

Monk-Warlock Synergy: Monks and Warlocks work well together as their shared reliance on technology unites them. When together and within melee range of each other, Monks and Warlocks can provide each other +1d6 to any check or save once per long rest each.
Wizard

The wizard of space is a master of alien technologies. Spending a lifetime searching for Alien artifacts and trying to understand them, the Wizard has gained technological powers so advanced they appear to be magic. The wizard’s spells are essentially various alien artifacts that happen to do exactly what that spell would do in normal D&D.
Alien Expert: Wizards have advantage on History or Investigation checks made to understand, find, or otherwise interact with alien artifacts.
Section Two: Redefining Races

The practical aspects of Races are completely unchanged. All the standard races still exist like normal, and simply have different lore and backstories. For races other than the most common ones, you are free to decide for yourselves.
Humans
Humans are completely the same. Originating from Earth, they are very common throughout the galaxy
Eldar (Elves)

The Eldar are an ancient race of humanoids from the planet Eldaran. They are tall, slender, and do not need sleep. Equal measures wise and xenophobic, the Eldar cooperate with Humans for their mutual benefit but have never fully trusted them. The uneasy alliance between the Eldar and the Humans has been enlightening, but tension remains present at all times
Half Elves
Eldar and Humans can somehow reproduce with one another, an incredible galactic coincidence. Their offspring are Half Eldar, who are often either respected diplomats or detested freaks.
Drukhari (Dark Eldar)

Long before humanity became a galactic superpower, a subsection of the Eldar, called the Drukhari, split from their ancestors and more or less formed a new race. This race, equivalent to Drow in D&D, is not trusted by humanity or their Eldar cousins.
Votaan (Dwarves)

The votaan are a distant ancestor of humanity that split away from them long ago. When aliens came to earth to build the pyramids, they took humans with them to use as slaves on their homeworld of Votaai Alpha. These humans, taken to a planet with significantly stronger gravity, evolved over many years to become short and stout as the gravity pulled them down hard. They would eventually overthrow their slave masters, and form a minor empire in the galactic north. Though they descend from humans, their customs, way of life, and appearance has become very different. Life post-slavery has made the Votaan a hardy and stiff people.
Nocturni (Tiefling)

The Nocturni people are a dark skinned, horned, and tailed humanoid race from the volcanic planet Nocturne. The harsh, fiery volcanoes of Nocturne caused the Nocturni to evolve defenses against the heat and the violent wildlife of the planet. The Nocturni are not interested in empires, and for the most part remain as an insular people on their majestic homeworld. Some will go out to roam the galaxy, usually as part of their sacred tradition of exploration, in which Nocturnis will pledge to go out into the galaxy and do some great deed to honor Nocturne.
Orak-Hai (Orcs)

The Orak-Hai are a muddy green skinned people from their homeworld Orakiah. They have long, sharp teeth, and a somewhat barbaric style of life. Their jungle homeworld is home to massive, dinosaur-like creatures and the Orak-Hai evolved their customs and bodies around survival on the planet. They are natural born explorers, and will happily take up hard jobs on freighters or other vessels as a way to travel the galaxy.
Dargonians (Dragonborn)

The Dargonians are a reptilian species from the lush world of Dargonus. They have a rich and unique culture, made up of many different noble houses. Each noble house of Dargonus has a unique history, but more importantly a unique elemental specialization. House Firaxis, for example, has a tradition in which they learn to breathe fire. Dargonians are very pragmatic and efficient, and often have strong governmental minds.
Saturnians and Uranians (Gnomes and Halflings)

The massive gas giants of Saturn and Uranus produced two unique variants of humans, the Saturnian and the Uranian. When it was discovered that gas at the interior of both planets was very useful for producing warp fuel, specialized high pressure facilities were designed and constructed deep within the gas giant. These facilities were so high pressure and so close to the center of the planets that their inhabitants over time would be physically compressed. As such, when hiring workers to work at these facilities, smaller humans were hired preferentially. Because leaving one of these facilities required a lengthy and potentially dangerous depressurisation process, many workers in these colonies would stay for many years, potentially their entire life. As a result, these facilities became isolated colonies with unique culture and inhabited exclusively by small humans. After many years of this, a strange example of human artificial selection led the workers in these colonies to have smaller and smaller children, eventually resulting in humans who are very small and strong.  The major difference between the saturnians and uranians is their culture. Unlike other races on this list, the saturnians and uranians are still humans, just a very unique version of them.
